issues.legal_issue: A conviction cannot be sustained on the accepted remainder of an integrated prosecution account when an appellate court rejects an essential part on which that remainder depends and the remainder has no independent basis in the prosecution case.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged an initial demand and payment, followed by a demand for and acceptance of a further payment as part of the same transaction.
The High Court rejected the allegation concerning the initial demand and payment but accepted the allegation that money was recovered from the accused.
The prosecution had not put forward the recovered amount as a separate demand independent of the rejected allegation.
The Supreme Court considered the prosecution account integrated and the accepted part dependent on the part the High Court had disbelieved.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that it was unsafe to sustain the conviction on the remaining part of the prosecution account, allowed the appeal, and set aside the conviction and sentences.
issues.legal_principle: Where the prosecution presents an integrated account, an appellate court cannot sustain a conviction on a part that depends on an essential allegation it has rejected, particularly by recasting the prosecution case on a basis the prosecution did not advance. The convictions involved charges under Section 161 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 5(1)(d) and 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, but the Court applied no separate interpretive rule under those provisions and cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and prosecution_account_integrated and appellate_court_rejected_essential_part and accepted_part_depended_on_rejected_part and no_independent_prosecution_basis

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.prosecution_account_integrated: The prosecution presented the alleged demand and payments as connected parts of one transaction.
predicates.appellate_court_rejected_essential_part: The appellate court rejected an essential allegation in the prosecution account.
predicates.accepted_part_depended_on_rejected_part: The part accepted by the appellate court depended on the rejected allegation to support the alleged transaction.
predicates.no_independent_prosecution_basis: The prosecution did not advance the accepted part as an independent basis for the charged transaction.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a conviction concerns an integrated prosecution account whose accepted part depends on an essential rejected part and lacks an independent prosecution basis, the conviction and sentences are set aside.
